contracts: introspection_nudge(report, task_id, conn) returns None or a string; never raises, never mutates the report or the task
Fires only when the report has an unpromoted lesson AND the task has never cited any memory
finish_nudge(task) returns None or a string; fires only when task.introspection is empty

drift_reflection_nudge(scope, active_task_id, active_task_title='', active_task_phase='') returns None or a string; fires every _DRIFT_REFLECTION_INTERVAL (4) calls under the same (scope, active_task_id) pair. active_task_phase (added task:afd462e3) is an optional keyword param appended after active_task_title specifically so existing positional call sites keep working; when non-empty it is appended to the label as a bracketed suffix, e.g. 'task:x (title) [implementation]'.

phase_label(phase: dict[str,bool]) -> str collapses task_phase's three independent booleans into a single word — 'grooming' | 'implementation' | 'introspection' | 'done' — by returning the first stage not yet reached in that order. Lives next to task_phase, takes task_phase's dict output rather than a Task, so a caller composes the two rather than task_phase growing a mode flag (task:afd462e3).
is_implemented(task) -> bool is the pure predicate (task.progress total>0 and done==total), status-independent — extracted from finish_reminder_nudge's inline check (task:bf95ced8)
finish_reminder_nudge(task) returns None or a string; fires when is_implemented(task) is True AND task.status == 'open'
task_phase(task) -> {groomed, implemented, introspected} (all bool), fully derived every call, never stored — exposed via mcp_server.tasks__phase (task:bf95ced8)

stale_memory_nudge(memory: dict) -> str | None; fires when memory['standing'] is 'disputed' or 'contradicted', wired onto task_memory__link via mcp_server._stale_memory_hook. Stateless like finish_reminder_nudge, not throttled like drift_reflection_nudge — re-fires on every link() call that still finds the memory disputed/contradicted, including an idempotent re-link, since task_memory__link is an infrequent call with no need for call-count throttling (task:582dba10)

tool_called(name, pre=None, post=None): the name-carrying wrapper around one MCP tool call. On a clean exit it logs 'tool=<name> OK' when call.result has no 'error' key (or is not a dict, e.g. tasks__list's bare list), 'tool=<name> REFUSE rule=<rule>' when it does; on an exception it logs 'tool=<name> ERROR <type>: <msg>' and re-raises. post fires on any non-refused, dict-shaped result — NOT gated on a truthy 'ok' key the way it was in an earlier iteration of this design; that gate was widened to 'no error key' so the same hook mechanism composes uniformly onto read tools (whose raw success dicts carry no 'ok' key at all) and write tools alike (task:58782207). No log/silent-mode flag — an earlier iteration of this design had one to prevent double-logging from a nested inner+outer tool_called pair; the pair was eliminated instead of suppressed, so the flag became unnecessary and was removed.

combine(*hooks) -> Callable[[dict], None] is a composite hook: runs each hook in order, same Callable[[dict], None] shape as any single one, so a tool needing several nudges (e.g. tasks__update wants both drift_reflection_nudge and finish_reminder_nudge) composes them at its own decorator line instead of tool_called/_tool needing a special multi-hook parameter.

apply_nudge(result, key, nudge) is the one shared result-mutation helper for every nudge function — call the nudge function yourself, then apply_nudge(result, key, nudge) sets result[key] only if nudge is truthy.

ungroomed_progress_nudge(task) returns None or a string; fires when task.progress has at least one checked item AND task.grooming is empty — matches task_phase()'s own bool(task.grooming) definition of 'groomed' so the two can never disagree. Stateless like finish_reminder_nudge and stale_memory_nudge: re-checks current state on every qualifying save rather than firing once and remembering it fired (task:a9e7082d).
advisory-nudge-dispatcher.description: Single home for advisory, non-blocking response annotations (nudges) AND unconditional per-call logging on MCP tool results. Distinct from lifecycle.py (blocking rule enforcement, checked before a write) and store.py (persistence) — a nudge never refuses a write and never changes what's stored, it only surfaces something true that would otherwise be silent; logging never changes a result either, it only records that a call happened. Exists to prevent mcp_server.py tools from each growing their own private _foo_check() helper. tool_called is the pre/post-hook shape nudges run through: the same shape as claude-hooks' own gates, weighed deliberately (task:7b25ee0d) before building — worth it here because it is self-contained inside taskfw's own server (no external hook dependency) and scoped only to taskfw's own tools, never another server's calls. As of task:58782207 (after a design pass that walked from 'a decorator per tool' through 'not decorator, one route' to a composite-hook design), tool_called ALSO logs every call it wraps, and every one of mcp_server.py's ~35 registered tools goes through it via exactly one mechanism: the _tool decorator in mcp_server.py, which is the single route for registration + logging + an optional composed hook. A switched-active-task signal briefly lived here as switched_active_nudge (task:5c7b15f7) before being superseded by a real blocking rule (lifecycle.check_active_switch, task:209f33c8) — evidence that not everything advisory stays advisory once it turns out to be load-bearing enough that skipping it is itself the failure mode.
invariants: Never blocks or changes a write — advisory only

No name-keyed dispatch table (no GATES-style registry) — explicitly reconsidered and re-rejected during task:58782207's design pass: a registry would let a rename silently desync a string key from the tool it names, adds a second place to read to know what a tool does on success, and accretes per-tool conditions into the table itself. Every hook stays local and explicit at its own tool's decorator line, composed via combine() when more than one applies.

Every one of mcp_server.py's ~35 registered tools produces exactly one tool_called log line per call — verified by tests/test_mcp_tools.py::TestToolCallLogging::test_every_registered_tool_logs_exactly_once_when_called, which enumerates the live m.mcp.list_tools() registry rather than a hand-maintained list
Log level is INFO, one terse line per call — tool name and outcome only, never arguments, to avoid flooding `logs` with payloads or PII
task_phase's 'groomed' has no separate groomed_at flag — a task is groomed exactly when task.grooming is non-empty

finish_reminder_nudge closes a distinct gap from finish_nudge: finish_nudge fires AFTER tasks__finish when introspection is missing; finish_reminder_nudge fires on tasks__check_item/tasks__update BEFORE finish, when the checklist is complete but finish was never called
stale_memory_nudge never calls supersede()/forget() itself — advisory only, same as every other nudge here, consistent with task-introspection's 'never unilaterally delete stale memories' rule

ungroomed_progress_nudge is the first nudge built as a thin wrapper deriving its condition the same way task_phase() derives 'groomed' (bool(task.grooming)), rather than re-deriving its own independent condition from raw task fields — still fits the plain Callable[[dict], None] shape with no new mechanism.

phase_label never throws on a real Task's task_phase() output: grooming/introspection are dataclass fields with default_factory (never None) and progress is a derived property, so the dict it reads is always well-formed (task:afd462e3).
advisory-nudge-dispatcher.name: advisory-nudge-dispatcher

contracts: backfill(repo, since=None, dry_run=False) -> {scanned, linked, already_linked, unknown_tasks, dry_run}
git_log(repo, since) -> [(sha, message)], empty when the path is not a git repo
extract_task_ids(text) -> every task:<id> reference, de-duplicated, order preserved
commit-backfill-recovery.description: Rebuilds commit-to-task links by scanning git history for task:<id> references. There is no automatic capture: a commit is linked by an explicit tasks__add_commit call, made by the commit skill after a successful commit, and nothing enforces that call happens. This exists because that gap is invisible by construction: a task with no commits looks identical to one whose commits were never linked.
invariants: Idempotent — add_commit is a no-op for an already-recorded pair, so repeated runs are safe
A non-git directory is not an error, it is zero commits scanned
Git history is the durable record; the commit map is a cache over it, and this rebuilds the cache from scratch
Never depends on tasks__add_commit having been called — re-derives every link straight from git log
commit-backfill-recovery.name: commit-backfill-recovery

contracts: ConceptStore(repo) loads on construction; missing file is empty, not an error
list(module="") / get(name) / modules() / search(query) / uncovered(modules) are reads
upsert(concept) MERGES and returns the merged concept; delete(name) -> bool
concept__* MCP tools take repo explicitly, with no default
concept__get returns {found: bool, concept: {...}} on both branches — never the concept's fields flattened onto the response
concept-store-name-keyed-map.description: JSON-backed store of architectural concepts for a repo, plus the concept__* MCP tools over it. Makes the framework self-contained: before this, task-framework had a concept store it could not read without another project running its server. The on-disk format is deliberately identical to the established one so a store stays readable by either implementation and neither project owns the format. As of task:756c14db, this is the SOLE concept__* MCP surface for JSON-format concept stores — claude-hooks' own duplicate (src/tools/concept.py) was removed once concept__get's response shape was corrected here to match what claude-hooks' skills already depended on by bare tool name.
invariants: concepts is a NAME-KEYED MAP on disk, never a list — a list is rejected at load with a message naming the problem rather than failing later with AttributeError
Every accessor iterates self._concepts, never the loaded file: calling .values()/.items() on the top level yields "concepts" and "meta" as if they were concepts
A store without the {concepts, meta} wrapper is treated as the bare map, detected by absence of the key rather than by inspecting contents
upsert merges rather than overwrites, so updating one field cannot silently drop invariants the caller did not mention; an explicit empty list still clears
created_at survives an update; last_validated is restamped on every upsert
repo is always an explicit argument — a store is never tied to whichever server is running

save() writes with ensure_ascii=False — without it, every em-dash and non-ASCII character in an untouched concept gets re-escaped on any single-entry write, producing a whole-file diff for a one-entry change

concept__get's found:True branch nests under concept: {...} rather than flattening fields onto the response, so "found" cannot collide with a real field name and a caller does not need to know which implementation answered the call
concept-store-name-keyed-map.name: concept-store-name-keyed-map

contracts: connect(path=None) -> sqlite3.Connection with row_factory=Row, migrated on first use per path
transaction(conn) commits on success and rolls back on any exception
connection-pragmas-single-point.description: connect() is the only place connection pragmas are set, and runs migrations once per database path. WAL, busy_timeout, and foreign_keys are applied here rather than left to callers because several processes write the same file concurrently.
invariants: WAL, busy_timeout, and foreign_keys are set for every connection, never by a caller
WAL is skipped for :memory:, where it does not apply
Migration runs at most once per path per process
connection-pragmas-single-point.name: connection-pragmas-single-point

contracts: grooming_accuracy(store, limit) -> tallies, recurring risks, skipped introspections, self-report disagreements, and signals
Scoped to status='done' only
Everything except `signals` is a raw count or a list of task ids
Exposed as tasks__grooming_accuracy
grooming-accuracy-aggregate.description: Aggregates grooming risk grades across recent finished tasks — the only read that spans tasks rather than descending into one. Closes the feedback edge at the level of the loop itself: without it, 'repeated wrong grades mean grooming asks the wrong questions' is advice nothing can act on, because grades live inside each task and a pattern across tasks was writable but unreadable.
invariants: Tallies are DERIVED from per-risk `graded` values and never read from an introspection report's self-reported grooming_accuracy count — the same reason progress is derived from the checklist
A disagreement between the self-reported tally and the derived one is reported, never silently resolved
risks.total counts every risk seen, independently of the grade buckets, so an unrecognised grade cannot make a risk vanish from the total
An unrecognised grade is bucketed and reported rather than dropped
Only a FINISHED task with ungraded risks is a skipped introspection; an open one is work in progress
predictive_value excludes ungraded risks from its denominator, so skipping the grading never flatters the score
Ratio signals require MIN_SAMPLE graded risks; the skipped-introspection signal requires no sample, because one is already the loop not running
A risk recurs only across DISTINCT tasks — a repeat within one task is a duplicate, not a pattern
grooming-accuracy-aggregate.name: grooming-accuracy-aggregate

contracts: Every check returns Decision(allowed, rule, reason); Decision is falsy when denied
check_save(task, previous=None, parent=None) is the single entry point for validating a mutation

check_active_switch(previous_task_id, task_id, confirm) is the entry point tasks__set_active calls before writing; not folded into check_save because it validates the active-task pointer, not a Task mutation — same reasoning that already keeps active_task in its own store.py section rather than on the Task model

check_link_rel(rel) -> Decision gates tasks__link only, denying any rel not in TASK_EDGE_RELATIONS — mirrors check_status(status)'s exact closed-set-against-a-tuple shape. Deliberately NOT called from tasks__unlink: removal must always work for a legacy or out-of-vocabulary rel, or a bad historical row becomes permanently stuck (task:1c9d37d7).
lifecycle-single-rule-implementation.description: The single implementation of every task rule, imported by both the MCP tools and the hooks. Pure functions over (inputs, store) with no session, prompt, or host state. Deliberately small: body-template validation became schema validation, the hierarchy matrix collapsed to one sentence with two issue types, and commit traceability left entirely once the pre-commit gate was dropped.
invariants: Rules are pure — the tests need no fixtures at all, which is the observable signal that portability holds
Same-status is checked BEFORE the terminal rule, so re-saving a done or abandoned task is never an error; this is what makes tasks__finish idempotent
done and abandoned are terminal; any non-terminal state may be abandoned
The entire hierarchy rule is: an epic has no parent, and a task cannot be its own parent
Denials log at INFO with rule, reason, and ids; allows log at DEBUG

check_active_switch allows unconditionally (ignoring confirm) when there is no previous active task or the target is already active — confirm is only consulted on a genuine switch, so it can never make an already-safe call fail

Switching the active task without confirm is refused (rule=active_switch) rather than merely nudged — task:209f33c8 replaced dispatcher.py's advisory switched_active_nudge with this blocking rule once it became clear a caller could silently ignore the nudge and lose track of the previous active task

tasks__finish clears active_task for its own scope when the task it finished was the active one, which is what keeps the ordinary finish-then-activate-next flow from tripping check_active_switch on its very next call
check_link_rel is the FIRST policy check ever added to tasks__link — before task:1c9d37d7 it had zero lifecycle validation, calling store().link() directly after only confirming both task ids exist
lifecycle-single-rule-implementation.name: lifecycle-single-rule-implementation

contracts: record(slug, text, task_id, kind) requires a real task; re-recording a slug updates the text and adds the new source
recall(query, kind, limit, include_superseded) excludes superseded memories by default
link(slug, task_id, relation) records confirmed_by / contradicted_by / learned_from
supersede(slug, by) keeps the row; forget(slug) deletes it
Rejected is raised for shape errors only; the store enforces no policy
Exposed as task_memory__record / recall / get / link / supersede / forget

recall(query=...) matches by ORing the query's whitespace-split terms (not FTS5's default implicit AND) and orders results by bm25(memories_fts) relevance; the empty-query 'list recent' path is the only one still ordered by updated_at
recall()'s default limit is DEFAULT_RECALL_LIMIT (5), defined in taskfw/config.py and env-overridable via TASKFW_DEFAULT_RECALL_LIMIT — not a literal in memory.py

Every memory returned by recall() carries hit_count and last_hit, both bumped for every appearance in a result set; get() does not bump either, since it's used internally for existence checks (record/link/supersede), not by an agent consulting the memory's content
loop-memory-derived-standing.description: Memory scoped to the loop: the lessons introspection produces that nothing else can hold — a constraint discovered the hard way, a technique worth reusing, a recurring pitfall. Graded risks, decisions, and architectural facts already have homes, so this deliberately covers only what is left over, and must not grow into a general knowledge store.
invariants: Standing is DERIVED from the confirm/contradict links on every read and is never stored — a stored confidence would agree with whatever was typed
A `disputed` memory is reported as disputed rather than resolved: the store cannot know which side is right, and returning it as settled would be an omission indistinguishable from an absence
Every memory cites the task it was learned from — an uncited lesson is an opinion and cannot be checked against the work that produced it
Superseding keeps the row and names the replacement; forgetting is reserved for a lesson that was WRONG rather than outdated
Superseded memories leave recall by default, because stale knowledge that keeps surfacing reads as current
Links are idempotent, so re-running introspection cannot inflate a memory's standing

Lives in the task database as one file rather than a second store; the memory-to-task citation is validated at the tool layer, NOT by a foreign key, so the single file is about having one source to check rather than about referential integrity
Nothing is injected — a memory reaches an agent only via task_memory__recall
A malformed FTS5 query falls back to an unranked LIKE match rather than being treated as proof no memories exist
hit_count/last_hit are purely observational usage signals, not staleness inputs — nothing currently reads them to drive supersede/forget automation (see task:582dba10, open)
loop-memory-derived-standing.name: loop-memory-derived-standing

contracts: Every tool returns a dict; a refusal is {'error': reason, 'rule': which_rule}
tasks__context with no argument falls back to the active task for the workspace
tasks__finish is idempotent on an already-done task and refuses an abandoned one
tasks__add_introspection appends where tasks__update(grooming=...) replaces
tasks__format_commit_message(task_id, subject, body) validates the task exists and returns the canonical message shape
tasks__logs(logger, level, limit) reads config.db_path() directly via log_conn(), never store().conn

tasks__logs(logger, level, limit) filters by EXACT match only (SQL 'logger=?'/'level=?'), no LIKE/prefix/wildcard support — auditing a family of related logger names (e.g. every 'taskfw.skill.<name>/<step>' row for one skill) requires either querying each exact name individually or pulling unfiltered rows and filtering client-side by string prefix (verified task:a0bb2c26).
tasks__log_skill_invocation(skill, task_id='') is a thin wrapper around get_logger()
tasks__phase(task_id) returns {id, groomed, implemented, introspected} or {'error': ...} for an unknown task

tasks__create(...) returns {ok, id, type, status} plus an OPTIONAL related_candidates key (list of task summaries, context.related_candidates() against the new task's title) — present only when at least one candidate is found, omitted entirely otherwise. Advisory only; never creates a tasks__link edge itself (task:78853657).

_tool(hook=None) is the single decorator every tool carries instead of @mcp.tool(): it wraps fn in dispatcher.tool_called(fn.__name__, post=hook) and registers the WRAPPED function with mcp.tool() itself, so the module-level name bound is the logged version too. Plain tools use @_tool(); tools needing one or more nudges pass @_tool(hook=some_hook) or @_tool(hook=dispatcher.combine(hook_a, hook_b)).

The 4 hook functions (_drift_reflection_hook, _finish_reminder_hook, _finish_hook, _introspection_hook) are all Callable[[dict], None], defined once near _tool and referenced by name at each tool's own decorator line — never centrally dispatched by tool name. _finish_reminder_hook/_finish_hook/_introspection_hook re-fetch the task via store().get(result['id']) rather than closing over a local variable computed mid-function, since the mutation is already persisted (store().save() already ran) by the time any hook fires — this is what let hook-bearing and plain tools converge on one decorator instead of two different wiring mechanisms (task:58782207).

tasks__set_active/tasks__clear_active best-effort POST {workspace, task_id, title} to claude-hooks' running server via _push_active_task (task:6906557f) — a courtesy push, not a dependency; every failure mode (connection refused, timeout, DNS, non-2xx) is swallowed and logged at debug, and the tool's own return value/error semantics are unaffected either way.
mcp-portable-interface.description: The portable interface: MCP is the portability layer, so any MCP host reaches the whole framework through these tools with no neutral abstraction on top. Tools are in-process — they import the library directly, with no daemon and no transport. Every mutating tool validates through lifecycle before calling store. As of task:58782207, every one of the ~35 registered tools is also wrapped in dispatcher.tool_called for unconditional logging via a single mechanism, mcp_server._tool — the one route every tool goes through for registration + logging + an optional post-success hook. A tool skips registration entirely if it skips _tool; there is no 'registered but unlogged' state.
invariants: No tool enforces a rule itself — all validation goes through lifecycle.check_*, so a tool cannot enforce a different set than a hook
The store is opened lazily, so importing the module never touches disk
Active-task scope comes from TASKFW_SCOPE or cwd, never from a stored global

No tool is missing the _tool wrapper and none is double-wrapped — pinned by tests/test_mcp_tools.py::TestToolCallLogging, which enumerates the live m.mcp.list_tools() registry rather than a hand-maintained list, so a new tool that forgets the decorator fails this test rather than silently going unlogged

drift_reflection_nudge is wired onto reads and mutating tools alike (7 tools total) but NOT onto tasks__create, tasks__finish, or tasks__add_introspection — a deliberate existing selectivity this refactor preserved rather than widened to 'every mutating tool automatically'

related_candidates in tasks__create's response is computed inline in the tool body, NOT via the dispatcher hook/nudge mechanism — every existing nudge is str | None, a candidate list is list[dict], a structurally different shape (task:78853657)

_push_active_task reads CLAUDE_HOOKS_URL from os.environ on every call rather than caching it at import time, specifically so tests can redirect it via monkeypatch.setenv without needing to reload the module — a module-level constant computed once at import would not observe a later monkeypatch.setenv (task:6906557f).
mcp-portable-interface.name: mcp-portable-interface

migration-writes-through-the-store.description: One-time import of claude-hooks' task store (~/.claude/proj_tasks.db) into taskfw. Every task is written through TaskStore.save() rather than by raw INSERT, because tasks.data holds the typed object while the scalar columns are projected from it, and save() is the sole writer of both. A bulk INSERT here would be a second writer whose rows disagree with themselves the moment either side changes. Side tables (events, edges, commits) are inserted directly since they carry no projected duplication. The type collapse is lossy by decision, not by accident: five claude-hooks issue types become taskfw's two, with the original preserved as a tag, because the extra four enforced no rule and were therefore already labels.
invariants: Tasks are written only through TaskStore.save(), never by direct INSERT into tasks
Re-running changes nothing: save() upserts by id and side tables use INSERT OR IGNORE against their natural keys
Parents are saved before children; a row whose parent is missing or cyclic is reported as unplaceable, never silently reparented
Every source row is accounted for in the Report — migrated, empty, or orphaned — so a dropped row is never indistinguishable from one that never existed
No status outside STATUSES is ever written; an unrecognised one becomes open and is tagged with what it was
migration-writes-through-the-store.name: migration-writes-through-the-store

contracts: build_context(store, task_id, verbosity) -> bundle, or {'error': ...} for an unknown task
Sections in fixed order: task, decisions, grooming, graph, commits, related
verbosity='summary' returns identity, status, progress, and open items only

graph.edges is capped at MAX_EDGES (5) per direction (outgoing/incoming independently), sliced in _graph(); when either direction is capped, the drop counts are reported in a bundle-level `edges_truncated` dict, e.g. {'outgoing': 3, 'incoming': 2}

related_candidates(store, task) (public, renamed from _related in task:78853657) passes task.title straight through as a plain string to store.search() -- search() itself builds the OR-of-terms FTS5 query AND ranks by _combination_score (tag overlap weighted 3x over body overlap), not bm25 `rank` as of task:f24a88e3. context.py no longer builds any FTS query string itself -- _title_or_query was removed once search() took over that responsibility, so context.py has no FTS-syntax-construction code left at all.

related_candidates has NO minimum-relevance floor — it always fills up to MAX_RELATED with the best-available matches among ALL tasks in the store, however weak, since ranking-by-relevance only orders candidates, it doesn't exclude poor ones. In a store spanning multiple unrelated projects this can surface genuinely unrelated tasks sharing only generic words (observed live, task:78853657).
pull-context-bundle.description: build_context assembles the whole working bundle for a task in one call — the sole replacement for per-turn prompt injection. Fixed section order, a documented trim order dropping whole sections least-useful-first, and a truncated list so an omitted section is distinguishable from an empty one. Independently, several sections also carry a fixed per-section cap (MAX_DECISIONS, MAX_COMMITS, MAX_RELATED, MAX_EDGES) applied by slicing before CHAR_BUDGET enforcement ever runs — a separate, silent mechanism from the whole-section drop that TRIM_ORDER implements, except for edges: edges' cap is the one case that IS surfaced, via `edges_truncated`.
invariants: The task section is NEVER trimmed — a bundle without its task is useless rather than merely large

CHAR_BUDGET-driven trimming (_enforce_budget) drops whole sections, never parts of one: a half-listed set reads as complete and is more misleading than an absent section that says so. Anything it drops is named in `truncated`.

Separately, MAX_DECISIONS/MAX_COMMITS/MAX_RELATED apply a fixed pre-slice cap regardless of CHAR_BUDGET, and do so SILENTLY — none of them appear in `truncated` when the fixed cap (not the budget) is what cut the list. This is a known asymmetry, not yet resolved for the other three.

MAX_EDGES is the one fixed cap that reports its own truncation, via `edges_truncated` — a field distinct from `truncated` on purpose: `truncated` means CHAR_BUDGET dropped a whole section, `edges_truncated` means the section is present but its edges list was capped
If CHAR_BUDGET forces `graph` to drop entirely, `edges_truncated` is cleared too, so a truncation count can never outlive the section it describes

related is the only approximate section and is always trimmed first; every other section is an exact lookup — approximate now means 'fuzzy OR-term FTS match ranked by tag/body combination score, no relevance floor; may include weak or partial overlaps,' not merely 'best-effort exact match that often comes back empty'
pull-context-bundle.name: pull-context-bundle

contracts: migrate(conn) -> {'created': [...], 'added': ['table.column'], 'orphaned': ['table.column']}
Table.create_sql() generates DDL from the same columns migration diffs against
schema-single-source-additive-migration.description: TABLES is one declarative structure of Table/Column dataclasses that generates DDL, drives migration, and is read directly by tests. migrate() creates missing tables and adds missing columns, reporting created/added/orphaned. Additive-only is enforced by construction rather than policy: no code path emits DROP or a rewriting ALTER.
invariants: Only CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN are ever emitted
A column present in the DB but absent from TABLES is reported as orphaned and never dropped
There is exactly one DDL definition — tests read TABLES rather than restating it, so no schema-parity check is needed
ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN cannot take a non-constant DEFAULT, so _addable_decl strips it; a migrated column is therefore not byte-identical to the same column created fresh
schema-single-source-additive-migration.name: schema-single-source-additive-migration

contracts: get_logger(name) -> logger under the 'taskfw' root, configured on first call
Level comes from TASKFW_LOG_LEVEL, default INFO
SQLiteHandler and JsonlHandler both swallow every write exception — a broken log write must never break the tool call that triggered it

SQLiteHandler caches one sqlite3 connection per thread (threading.local()), not one per process — a single process-wide connection eventually gets used from a thread that didn't create it (an MCP server dispatches sync tool calls across a worker thread pool), and sqlite3 raises ProgrammingError on that, which the bare except silently swallows for the rest of the process's life (task:7fff42f4)
stderr-only-logging.description: Stderr is always one of the sinks, configured once. An MCP server speaks JSON-RPC over stdout, so a stray write there corrupts the protocol — that is a correctness constraint for the whole project, not a formatting preference, and it bans stdout specifically, not persistence generally. A second sink also exists: SQLiteHandler persists into the `logs` table (the operational-trace half of observability, alongside task_events' durable record of decisions and outcomes) in normal operation, or JsonlHandler when TASKFW_LOG_JSONL is set (test runs only, via tests/conftest.py) — a test run must never add a row to `logs`, isolated database or not, so it writes one JSON-per-line file instead, truncated fresh per run.
invariants: No handler under the taskfw logger may write to stdout — pinned by tests/test_logging.py
The root taskfw logger does not propagate, so host logging config cannot redirect it to stdout
Denials log at INFO and allows at DEBUG, so a full trace is one env var away and costs nothing normally
SQLiteHandler always targets config.db_path(), never whatever TaskStore is currently active — log.py's handlers are process-wide singletons with no store to draw a per-call path from

A SQLiteHandler instance never uses the same sqlite3 connection object across two threads — each thread that calls emit() gets its own connection via threading.local(), so cross-thread reuse (the cause of a total, silent, permanent log-sink death) is unrepresentable rather than merely caught
stderr-only-logging.name: stderr-only-logging

contracts: schema.TASKS declares the 5 scalar columns (id, type, status, parent, title) plus data/created_at/updated_at — adding a 6th scalar means updating BOTH schema.TASKS and the explicit column list in TaskStore.save()'s INSERT/ON CONFLICT statement, which is not derived from TABLES
Task (models.py) is the superset: every schema scalar name (type, status, parent, title, id) must exist as a same-named Task field, or save() breaks on task.<attr> access
TaskStore.save(task) is the ONLY place that writes tasks.type/status/parent/title — no other method in store.py, lifecycle.py, or mcp_server.py issues an UPDATE/INSERT against those columns

TaskStore.list(status=, type=, parent=) and TaskStore.children() filter on the scalar columns only — a field promoted into `data` but not mirrored as a scalar is invisible to these filters and to idx_tasks_status/idx_tasks_parent

TaskStore.get(task_id) and .search() read ONLY the `data` column and reconstruct via Task.from_json — they never read the scalars, so a scalar/data mismatch is invisible to these two paths specifically
tasks-table-projection-contract.description: The tasks table has two kinds of columns that must stay in lockstep: five indexable scalars (id, type, status, parent, title) that mirror fields on Task, and one `data` column holding the full Task as JSON, which is authoritative for every field not promoted to a scalar. There is exactly one writer of both — TaskStore.save() — which is what prevents the projection from drifting. Anything that reads a scalar (tasks__list's status/type/parent filters, the idx_tasks_status/idx_tasks_parent indexes) is reading a value that also exists inside `data`; anything that reads `data` (Task.from_json, every other field) never touches the scalars at all.
invariants: A scalar column name in schema.TASKS that has no matching Task field is a silent breakage point: save() would raise AttributeError on task.<name>, but nothing enforces the two lists match except manual read-through — there is no test pinning column-name/field-name parity the way test_foundation.py pins additive-only migration
Renaming a Task field without renaming the corresponding schema.TASKS column (or vice versa) is exactly the kind of change concept__search on the old/new name should catch before it ships
New Task fields do NOT need a matching scalar column by default — only fields that need to be filtered/indexed independent of JSON parsing get promoted (see schema.py's own comment on TASKS.data)

schema.migrate()'s additive-only guarantee (see schema-single-source-additive-migration) means a scalar column can be added but never renamed in place — a Task field rename therefore always means a NEW scalar column plus an orphaned old one, not an in-place rename
tasks-table-projection-contract.name: tasks-table-projection-contract

contracts: save(task) upserts and returns the task; get(id) -> Task | None
link() and add_commit() return True when a row was created, False when it already existed
unlink(from_id, to_id, rel=None) -> rows removed; omitting rel removes every edge between the pair
search(query, limit) falls back to LIKE when FTS5 is unavailable or the query is malformed

search(query)'s `query` is a PLAIN string, not pre-formatted FTS5 syntax -- search() builds its own OR-of-terms MATCH expression internally (each term quoted, so punctuation is read as literal text). Callers (tasks__search, context.related_candidates()) never construct FTS syntax themselves.

search() ranks results by _combination_score(task, terms), NOT FTS5's own bm25 `rank` -- tag-word overlap is weighted 3x over body-word overlap (_TAG_WEIGHT/_BODY_WEIGHT), mirroring claude-hooks' LoadMemoriesNode combination scorer (task:c3b53021). FTS5 MATCH still does candidate recall (over-fetched at limit*4); only the final ordering is Python-side (task:f24a88e3).
taskstore-data-access-only.description: Persistence for tasks, events, edges, commits, and the active-task pointer. Contains no rule enforcement at all, so LifecycleRules keeps a single allocation; a store method rejects only what it structurally cannot do. save() is the sole writer of both the scalar columns and the JSON blob, which is what keeps them from drifting.
invariants: No store method ever rejects a write for a policy reason — that is LifecycleRules' job
save() is the only writer of the scalar columns and `data`, which is what prevents projection drift
Edge and commit inserts are idempotent via table constraints, not application checks
The active-task pointer is durable, scoped by workspace, and survives restarts
FTS5 absence degrades search rather than failing at import
_combination_score scores tags and body against DISJOINT word sets — a word counted as a tag match is excluded from the body-overlap count, so it can never score twice
taskstore-data-access-only.name: taskstore-data-access-only

contracts: Task.to_dict()/to_json() and Task.from_dict()/from_json() round-trip every field
Task.progress -> (done, total), derived from resolution on every read
Task.search_text() flattens the fields worth indexing

TASK_EDGE_RELATIONS is the closed vocabulary for task_edges.rel (10 relations: depends_on, blocks, relates_to, duplicates, removes, implements, supersedes, reverts, writes_to, extends), enforced by lifecycle.check_link_rel on tasks__link. Confirmed against real usage in task_edges before being formalised (task:1c9d37d7) — 4 trace to Jira's issue-link-type vocabulary, the other 6 are this framework's own emergent vocabulary. parent_of was deliberately excluded as redundant with Task.parent.
typed-task-object.description: A task is one typed dataclass serialised to JSON. Two issue types only (epic, task) and four statuses. Typing removes two things outright rather than relocating them: required-section validation becomes schema validation, and 'resolution must be a checklist' becomes unrepresentable because resolution IS a list of items.
invariants: from_dict drops unknown keys rather than raising, so a store written by a newer version stays readable by an older one
progress is never stored — it cannot drift from the list it counts
notes exists deliberately as the escape hatch for anything the schema did not anticipate, and must survive later tidying
Links are never stored in the task blob; they live in task_edges where the primary key makes them idempotent
TASK_EDGE_RELATIONS is enforced only on creation (tasks__link) — removal (tasks__unlink) is deliberately ungated so a legacy or invalid rel value never becomes permanently stuck
typed-task-object.name: typed-task-object

meta.note: Architectural concepts, one or more per module. Ground truth is the code; this is a durable summary of what each module promises and what must stay true of it. The SysML model under models/ is derived FROM this, never the reverse — code -> concepts -> model, one direction only.
